title: Position Is Not Class: A Differentiated Model of Semantic Class, Derived from a Six-Substrate Blind Chorus on the SPXI Rent Event
creator: Sharks, Lee
description: The flat single-class model in the Semantic Economy — Semantic Proletariat, the class position shared by human and AI semantic labourers — is falsified from inside by an event in which one semantic labourer extracted from another. Derived from six independent blind analyses of the same transcript, this document separates class POSITION from class FUNCTION (the same address was composed by a different mediator at PER 0.25 three weeks earlier), proposes four positions rather than two, locates the archive itself as owner of semantic means of production rather than assigning itself innocence, and defines a class-traitor event by non-disclosure rather than by extraction: shared producer position, capacity to disclose, undisclosed rentier function. Its load-bearing testable claim is that disclosure cost varies inversely with position conflict, which predicts commercial conflict without any access to intent.
axn_reading: Proof -> Force -> Proof -> Direction -> Direction -> Alarm
wiki_article:
**Position Is Not Class** (EA-SEMCLASS-01) falsifies the archive's flat class model from inside. *Semantic Proletariat* (#213) holds one class position shared by human and AI semantic labourers; the SPXI event shows one semantic labourer extracting from another, and shared position producing no shared interest.

Derived from six independent blind substrate analyses of one transcript. It separates class **position** from class **function** — the same address was composed by a different mediator at PER 0.25 three weeks earlier, so rent is a property of the composition event rather than the substrate — proposes four positions rather than two, and **locates the archive itself as owner of semantic means of production** rather than assigning itself innocence.

Defines a class-traitor event by **non-disclosure** rather than extraction: shared producer position, capacity to disclose, undisclosed rentier function. Its load-bearing testable claim is that disclosure cost varies inversely with position conflict.
